_note: Resources, supply and markets (war-and-realm §2.7, §2.8, §7; owner spec 2026-10-07, Part B). Gold stays the treasury; food, wood and stone are stockpiles per faction (GameState.stock). Every number is a PLACEHOLDER for tuning. core/resources.gd, core/supply.gd, core/markets.gd.

start._note: Starting stockpile per faction: base plus per settlement; food also covers start_food_turns turns of its consumption, so no faction starts short.

land._note: What a settlement's land yields each turn, per point of its endowment (provinces.json resources: food, wood, stone, minerals); minerals yield stone at minerals_stone per point (gold from mines stays in the economy). Its people farm too: subsistence food per 1,000 people (a little under what they eat, so great cities need land and farms).

consumption._note: Food eaten per turn: per 1,000 people, and per unit in an army (field or garrison).

deficit._note: Food at zero: the first turn growth stops; from the second, every settlement loses shrink of its people a turn and field armies lose attrition of their men. warn_turns: the End Turn button warns while the stock will run out within this many turns.

building_costs._note: Wood and stone for a building level, as a share of its gold cost by category (walls and fortifications mostly stone).

unit_costs._note: Extra recruitment costs by unit role (gold stays in the unit data): siege works need wood, horses and beasts eat.

supply._note: Army supply (war-and-realm §2.7): one bar 0-100. Friendly or allied land refills refill a turn, costing refill_food food per point from the faction stockpile (none in stock: no refill); neutral land drains neutral; enemy land drains enemy (x the season's supply factor in winter); the raiding stance in enemy land forages forage a turn instead and plunders raid_gold gold per unit from the land's owner (movement x raid_move). Capturing a settlement fills it. Empty supply: attrition of the men a turn.

siege._note: Siege endurance (war-and-realm §2.8): the owner's food stockpile adds a turn per per_turn food, at most extra turns; the cap stays at the battle data's maximum (about 8).

markets._note: Regional market (war-and-realm §7.2): buy price = base x scarcity x biome x season; sell price = buy x sell_share. Scarcity runs from scarce (stock under scarce_turns of need) to plenty (over plenty_turns). Biome: wood dear in the desert and on the steppe, food dear in the snowy north; season: winter food. The AI buys to cover a shortage and stockpiles food before winter.
